study: Landry et al. 2014, Responsive Early Childhood Program (RECC/RECC+), toddler care (Developmental Psychology)
eval_evidence: Authored and conducted by the program's research team (Landry/Children's Learning Institute and collaborators); RECC and the responsive-teaching PD are the authors' own program (NICHD P01 HD048497).
developer_evidence: Coaches who delivered the responsive-teaching PD/curriculum were selected and 'systematically trained to deliver the intervention by the principal investigator and supervisor' and supervised by senior research staff (p.~533-536).
cascade_evidence: Project coaches (research-team staff trained and supervised by the PI/senior research staff) work directly with intervention teachers; not a school-system lead-teacher train-the-trainer cascade.
counterfactual_evidence: Control condition 'received no training or curriculum' (only data-submission stipends); business-as-usual is the stated control arm (p.~518; abstract/methods).
coaching_evidence: Teachers received weekly in-class coaching for 9 months (37 weeks), ~20 in-class sessions; described as relatively high-demand 'weekly coaching sessions across 37 weeks' (p.538-539, 1665).
student_dose_evidence: Intervention = curriculum + teacher coaching changing the teacher's own instruction; no tutoring/pull-out/software dose delivered to children. (RECC+ adds a teacher-delivered SE supplement, still teacher-mediated.)
maturity_evidence: Each cohort received the program across one academic year (37-week school year) with child outcomes measured pre-post within that year; no multi-year maturation axis (multiple cohorts are staggered single-year implementations).
